# Representation and whole-scope limits of the bulk theorem

This note supplements the fixed-width upgrade without changing the preserved initial derivation.

## Polynomial growth of the receiving function

All retained slopes are in [-1,0]^d, and the all-ones vector is in the plateau for sufficiently large R. Thus L_i(1)>=M_(1/R), and for x>=0 with max x_i=N,

    M_(1/R)-L_i(x) <= -r_i.(x-1) <= d N.

Consequently 0<=U_R(x)<=dN+theta log m. The weights R^p up to R=(2N)^(1/H) sum to O(N^(p/H)), and the remainder has the locally convergent exponential bound already proved. Therefore

    V(x) <= C(1+N)^(p/H+1).

The matching-scale argument gives a polynomial lower bound tending to infinity. These are graph/class/rate-dependent abstract constants, potentially enormous. This is a polynomial-growth Foster FUNCTION in the fixed-width bulk, not a polynomial-time algorithm or a stationary-tail theorem.

## Effective acquisition remains separate

The external finite affine-family theorem is an existence construction involving limiting activity sets and a finite subcover. Its public successor explicitly distinguishes this from an efficient numerical extraction of slopes or H. The present abstract receiver uses the whole finite family as supplied by that proved mathematical lemma; it does not solve that separate effective-extraction problem. No executable instance of that entire family was emitted by `softmin_checks.py`.

Once actual affine data and evaluation access to its offsets are available, labels active in [1,R]^d are a finite linear-programming question, and a common Hoffman constant is a finite matrix error-bound calculation. The scale tail supplies a finite approximation rule for a specified x and error. This conditional evaluation fact is not a claim that the source family or its constants were numerically acquired in this run.

Hoffman's original *On Approximate Solutions of Systems of Linear Inequalities*, J. Research NBS 49 (1952), 263--265, proves the matrix-dependent uniform error bound used here. The proof removes right-hand sides by translation at a nearest face and takes a finite minimum over row subsets. Thus varying offsets and R do not introduce an uncharged R-dependent constant in the bulk argument. Primary source: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/jres/049/4/v49.n04.a05.pdf . # Fixed-width bulk upgrade

Author-derived and unaudited. This strengthens the weaker logarithmic-bulk construction in `BULK_CONSTRUCTION.md`; that file is preserved as the initial derivation. The global function, exact finite-jump bound, source-cut proof, classwise plateau exclusion, normalization and scale gluing remain the same. The improvement is a sharper use of the acquired active-region distance.

## Theorem

Subject to the governing finite affine-family lemma cited and read in the preceding construction, every finite weakly reversible mass-action network with fixed positive rates admits, on each positive affine compatibility class, a nonnegative normlike function V on the count orthant with

    L V(x)<=-1

outside a class-dependent finite set wherever EVERY coordinate is at least K=max(1,2D), where D is the largest source degree. The assertion covers arbitrary dimension and arbitrary linkage multiplicity. It is a BULK statement, not general recurrence: the union of excluded strips x_i<K is infinite. No bound uniform across conserved enzyme pools or actual communication classes is silently supplied.

If the compatibility class has no point with all coordinates >=1, its bulk is empty. Otherwise choose a single such c as the representative in the affine construction. A count state in the bulk has all sources enabled, and actual falling factorials are uniformly comparable to monomials. No high-volume or continuum limit occurs.

## The strengthened near-active calculation

Write n=min x_i, N=max x_i, R>=2N, and retain affine labels active somewhere in [1,R]^d as before. Their slopes are nonpositive, and the uniform Hoffman constant B is acquired from fixed coefficient matrices. Let

    ell=L log(2+N),

where L is a finite constant chosen below. Call a label near-active when its affine gap is at most ell. It has an actual active point z in [1,R]^d with

    |z-x|_infinity<=B ell.

Both x and z have every coordinate at least one. Hence, even when some x_i are bounded, every coordinate ratio between them is between

    1/(1+B ell) and 1+B ell.

The original derivation unnecessarily demanded a factor-two ratio, which required n to grow logarithmically. A polylogarithmic distortion is enough. If r_i.u<r_i.v, the primary source sign-gap lemma at z gives

    z^v/z^u<=R^(-H),
    x^v/x^u<=(1+B ell)^(|v-u|_1) R^(-H)
              <=(1+B ell)^(2D) R^(-H).

## Public primary sources

**OpenAI, Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems (October 5, 2026).** [Source directory](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints/Uniform-Permanence-in-Weakly-Reversible-Mass-Action-Systems-October-5-2026). The affine approximation, trapping and permanence sources were read. They supply the finite affine family, sign gap and plateau geometry used in the new bulk receiver. The theorem itself concerns deterministic concentration trajectories. The repository README describes mixed verification status; its [Lean scope note](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/docs/149.md) names the September 25 companion and its initial-state-dependent bounds. This run claims no new Lean verification or audited stochastic consequence. Exact connector-text copies and hashes are under `sources/connector/`.

**Michael Mislan, Endotactic permanence and quantitative recovery with vanishing reverse rates (Hexagon 2610.00321v1, October 20, 2026).** [Primary record](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00321v1), [uniform source](https://hexagonmath.org/api/v1/works/2610.00321v1/source?path=uniform.tex), [reverse source](https://hexagonmath.org/api/v1/works/2610.00321v1/source?path=reverse.tex). The governing deterministic witness/plateau proof and the stochastic section were inspected. This is the stronger ordinary deterministic successor: general endotacticity, bounded measurable rate histories and classwise absorption. Its stochastic section gives an inventory-based lower recovery-time comparison, and explicitly leaves positive recurrence of its four-linkage example open. It does not supply the finite-jump stochastic receiver developed here. Numerical extraction of its affine data is separately identified as unresolved.
